comparisons.peer_topic: Factors driving competition and workforce dependencies
comparisons.peer_summary: Competition relies on factors such as customer service, product pricing and quality, technology delivery, and reputation, while effective competition also depends on the ability to attract, retain, and motivate employees while managing compensation costs.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Bank of America identify asset management as a segment directly impacted by competitive and pricing dynamics driven by fee structures and investment strategies. GS explicitly cites the prevalence of passive strategies with lower fees affecting its asset management products (GS: "The increasing prevalence of passive investment strategies that typically have lower fees than other strategies we offer has affected the competitive and pricing dynamics for our asset management products and services."). BAC broadly identifies 'pricing' and 'product pricing' as a key factor of competition and notes in its summary that it faces competitive pressure in asset management. However, GS details the specific mechanism (passive investing fees) while BAC lists pricing as a general factor alongside customer service and technology.

sentences.text: The increasing prevalence of passive investment strategies that typically have lower fees than other strategies we offer has affected the competitive and pricing dynamics for our asset management products and services.

Competition is based on a number of factors including, among others, customer service and convenience, the pricing, quality and range of products and services offered, lending limits, the quality and delivery of our technology and our reputation, experience and relationships in relevant markets.

comparisons.peer_topic: Competitive landscape and basis of competition
comparisons.peer_summary: JPMorganChase operates in highly competitive environments, competing against a diverse range of financial and non-financial entities. The firm competes based on product quality, variety, innovation, reputation, and price, with competitive scope varying by client type and geography.
comparisons.comparison: Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase both describe a highly competitive environment where price is a significant basis for competition across their diverse businesses. GS notes that price competition has compressed bid/offer spreads affecting market-making, and generally faces pricing pressure (GS: "Price competition has also led to compression in the difference between the price at which a market participant is willing to sell an instrument and the price at which another market participant is willing to buy it... which has affected our market-making businesses." and "The increasing prevalence of passive investment strategies... has affected the competitive and pricing dynamics for our asset management products and services."). JPM explicitly states it competes on price and varies by product and geography (JPM: "The Firm's businesses generally compete on the basis of the quality and variety of the Firm's products and services, transaction execution, innovation, reputation and price." and "Competition also varies based on the types of clients, customers, industries and geographies served."). Both firms identify price/fees as a core competitive driver, though GS highlights the structural shift from passive investing while JPM lists price as one of several bases including innovation and quality.

sentences.text: Price competition has also led to compression in the difference between the price at which a market participant is willing to sell an instrument and the price at which another market participant is willing to buy it (i.e., bid/offer spread), which has affected our market-making businesses.

The increasing prevalence of passive investment strategies that typically have lower fees than other strategies we offer has affected the competitive and pricing dynamics for our asset management products and services.
The Firm's businesses generally compete on the basis of the quality and variety of the Firm's products and services, transaction execution, innovation, reputation and price.

comparisons.peer_summary: Competition is increasing globally from established and emerging firms, including non-financial companies focusing on technology innovation, which may be larger, better capitalized, or have stronger local presence, leading to enhanced product offerings and pricing pressure.
comparisons.comparison: Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley both identify intense price competition and pricing pressure as a key feature of their competitive landscape, particularly in market-making and asset management/wealth management contexts. GS reports that price competition has compressed bid/offer spreads and that passive investing has affected pricing dynamics in asset management (GS: "Price competition has also led to compression in the difference between the price at which a market participant is willing to sell an instrument and the price at which another market participant is willing to buy it..." and "The increasing prevalence of passive investment strategies... has affected the competitive and pricing dynamics for our asset management products and services."). MS highlights that increased competition from various firms results in 'additional pricing pressure' (MS: "Many of these firms have the ability to offer a wide range of products and services through different platforms that may enhance their competitive position and could result in additional pricing pressure on our businesses."). Both firms acknowledge pricing as a direct compressive force on revenue, whereas MS emphasizes the source of this pressure (non-financial tech firms and larger institutions) more than GS does in this specific sentence.

sentences.text: Price competition has also led to compression in the difference between the price at which a market participant is willing to sell an instrument and the price at which another market participant is willing to buy it (i.e., bid/offer spread), which has affected our market-making businesses.

The increasing prevalence of passive investment strategies that typically have lower fees than other strategies we offer has affected the competitive and pricing dynamics for our asset management products and services.

Many of these firms have the ability to offer a wide range of products and services through different platforms that may enhance their competitive position and could result in additional pricing pressure on our businesses.
